result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers place all eight pieces clearly, with proportions you could draw from. B makes alarms the biggest block, gives abnormal turbine tiles an icon and a word as well as colour, and sets out an explicit tier table for reading at 6 m, at 3 m and only up close. A explains well why curtailment and output belong together, but its alarm panel is slightly smaller than the turbine grid, and its banner grows when active, which shifts the layout. B keeps every panel a fixed size and adds stale-data handling, which suits a wall display better. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B wins narrowly. It gives width and height for every panel, so the layout can be drawn directly. It also states the important links outright: alarms and the turbine grid use the same colours, and curtailment explains why output is below forecast. A has the clearer table of what's readable from where and puts alarms in the biggest block, but its percentage sizes don't add up and it never explicitly links the alarm list to the turbine grid.
